GitHub pilot can validate action-bound personal consent, but it has no bounded operational publication path or concrete LD-07 acceptance request. This change adds a manual protected-main workflow, an allowlisted PR publisher scope and a separate pilot view that remains inactive until explicit personal operating acceptance is captured, independently checked and merged.

The LD-07 request binds the confirmed GRS-002/report-only scope, permitted operations, exclusions, implementation/toolchain fingerprints and operating runbook. It asks the named maintainer for a personal decision on this pilot; the channel-test comment, role appointment and technical merge exception do not supply acceptance. Individual decision/progress/closure statements remain required. Original validation receipts retain their labels and bytes; the new view explicitly records its promotion basis.

Missing, rejected, revoked, edited/deleted consent, withdrawn roles or an implementation mismatch prevent effective operation. Permission-reducing corrections remain publishable. New official projections recheck operating consent even when no new acceptance capture is added. The existing manual Governance CI dispatch now runs immutable-history and provider checks against main, so bot-created PRs receive the same admission checks. Quarantined evidence also hides an otherwise active closure in the projection.

The workflow has no schedule, executes no remediation, never posts personal consent and never pushes directly to main. It prepares observation, action, acceptance or refresh updates and submits only dedicated evidence/index/report paths through PR checks. Other consumers, baseline packages, Bitbucket and blocking enforcement are excluded.

Validation: pinned bootstrap/full validation (470 tests), strict MkDocs, 11 operating-acceptance tests, 13 publisher tests, 16 action tests and accepted-prefix/provider checks. No operating acceptance capture exists and the generated live pilot view is inactive. The first live workflow execution follows the maintainer's personal LD-07 decision.

The standing maintainer review exception authorizes the technical merge after required checks pass. Restore the exact original review rule immediately after merging. This PR merge does not constitute LD-07 acceptance.
